subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm checking the render against red panda identity cues — the tail looks too tall and thin like a scorpion's curl rather than the thick, horizontal droop of a real red panda, and I need to verify whether the tear marks and ear rim coloring are reading correctly on the face.

Looking more closely, the body proportions feel off too — it's a bit long and flat with tiny legs, and the scarf collar is creating problems: from the front it reads as a bulky teal hexagon/octagon shape around the head rather than a natural draped scarf, and the ribbon tails seem to sit awkwardly across the back and side instead of draping naturally. I think I need to shrink the scarf loop and rework how it loops around the body so it doesn't dominate the silhouette.

The tail also needs reshaping — it's currently too tall and thin, reading like a pillar standing behind the head and blocking it in the front view. I want to thicken the tail radius and curve it lower and to the side so it sweeps along near the ground instead of standing upright, while making sure it stays within the platform's radius so it doesn't extend off the stage edge.

Checking the eyes and face markings next — the eyebrow spots and cream/orange skull paint look right, matching a red panda's facial pattern well, and the legs are all consistently dark purple-maroon.

The moss blobs on the boulder look a bit cluttered but are stylized enough to keep, even though they partially hide the paws on top. I'm noticing a leaf card floating in front of the face in the front view, overlapping the chin, so I should filter out or reposition the leaves that interfere with the face.

Fixing the angle math so motes and leaves avoid the frontal arc near the face, shifting their placement toward the sides and back instead. The ear's inner color reads a bit gray-brown from cel-shading shadow rather than cream, but overall the ears look fine.

Adjusting the cheek ruff blade directions so they angle backward and downward more instead of sticking out horizontally like spikes, shortening their length and widening their thickness slightly for a better silhouette. Now I'm checking the scarf collar sizing against the body's width at that height to make sure the ring fits properly.

The head feels too small compared to the body for the chibi proportions I'm aiming for, so I'm weighing whether to scale the skull up by roughly 1.25x, which would cascade into adjusting muzzle, ear, and eye decal placements, versus the simpler alternative of shrinking the body's loft width instead to balance the proportions.

Scaling head geometry proportionally...

I should also shrink body proportions to keep the scarf and loft widths balanced, though leg and belt positions can stay fixed since they're independent. Now I need to introduce an HS scale factor into the H helper function so all head-relative coordinates scale consistently.

Next I'm reworking the tail — widening its radius curve and tip taper, increasing lateral curve detail, bumping the scatter count to 110, and adjusting the scatter filter threshold — before moving on to scale the skull dimensions.

Still editing ear and cheek blade specs...

Adjusting the mote angle distribution so they spread wider toward the sides and back, then double-checking the leaf card and scarf placements still work with the larger head before writing up the final answer.
